$comment: Local validation bundle from unapproved UCP PR 945; not a published extension.

target.description: What an operation applies to: the entire Order or one declared modification unit. Unknown `type` values MUST be rejected by Businesses and MUST NOT be interpreted by Platforms.

type.description: Target kind. Well-known values: `order` (the entire Order; `id` MUST be absent) and `unit` (a modification unit declared in `modification.units[]`; `id` is required).

id.description: Stable opaque unit identifier when `type` is `unit`. MUST NOT be interpreted as an array index or as a line item or payment-settlement identifier.

unit_target.description: Relationship between a modification unit and a visible Order component. A unit is a stable modification target, not necessarily an independent payment-settlement unit.

type.description: Kind of Order component. Well-known value: `line_item`. Platforms MUST tolerate unknown values.

quantity.description: Steps of the line item's quantity unit that this unit covers. Cancelling the unit cancels exactly this quantity; quantity-reduction requests are out of scope.

processing_mode.description: How the Business processes a cancellation. Well-known values: `immediate` (the Business decides and commits within the request) and `merchant_review` (the attempt is admitted and the Business decides later). Platforms MUST treat any unrecognized value as `merchant_review` and MUST NOT assume commitment.

operations.description: Supported operations. This draft defines only `cancel`. Platforms MUST ignore unknown values and MUST NOT submit an operation that is not listed.

order_cancellation.description: Whole-order cancellation metadata, declared whether or not whole-order cancellation is currently available and independent of `granularity`.

available.description: Whether whole-order cancellation is currently offered. MUST be true if and only if the enclosing `modification.operations` contains `cancel`.

processing_mode.description: Required when `available` is true, including when `granularity` is `by_unit`.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason whole-order cancellation is unavailable. Open vocabulary; clients MUST tolerate unknown values.

reversible_amount.description: Non-negative amount attributed to whole-order cancellation, in the Order's `currency` minor units. Attribution, not a settlement instruction.

estimated_refund_amount.description: Non-negative estimated refund for whole-order cancellation in the Order's `currency` minor units. Omitted means unknown, not zero; the estimate is not a guarantee and MAY differ from the final `adjustments[]` value.

unit.description: An independently addressable modification unit declared on the authoritative Order read.

id.description: Stable opaque unit identifier, unique within the Order. Unchanged while the unit remains addressable.

targets.description: Order components the unit maps to, with the quantities it covers.

operations.description: Operations currently supported on this unit. An empty array means the unit is declared but not currently modifiable; `reason_code` SHOULD explain.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason the unit is unavailable. Open vocabulary; clients MUST tolerate unknown values.

reversible_amount.description: Non-negative amount attributed to the unit in the Order's `currency` minor units. A pooled payment does not make unit attribution impossible.

estimated_refund_amount.description: Non-negative estimated refund for cancelling the unit. Omitted means unknown, not zero; not a guarantee and distinct from the final adjustment.

modification_declaration.description: Authoritative, response-only declaration of what post-purchase modification the Business supports for this Order at this `order_version`. Its presence means the extension is negotiated; absence means the Platform MUST NOT infer programmatic cancellation support. An Order-only implementation declares `granularity: order_only` explicitly.

granularity.description: Addressing granularity. Well-known values: `order_only` (only whole-order operations; `units` MUST be absent or empty) and `by_unit` (independently addressable `units[]` are declared). Open vocabulary: a Platform that does not recognize the value MUST NOT address units and MAY submit only a whole-order operation when `order_cancellation.available` is true.

atomicity.description: Order mutation commitment model. Well-known values: `atomic` (all operations of one attempt commit as one all-or-nothing mutation) and `per_unit` (independently eligible units commit and fail independently). Applies to Order mutation commitment, not to downstream financial settlement. Open vocabulary: a Platform that does not recognize the value MUST submit single-operation requests only and MUST treat any result other than `committed` as unresolved.

operations.description: Supported Order-level operations. MUST contain `cancel` if and only if `order_cancellation.available` is true.

units.description: Independently addressable modification units. Required when `granularity` is `by_unit`.

order_version.description: Opaque Order state version. The Business MUST change it whenever any Platform-visible part of the Order changes (line quantities, fulfillment events, adjustments, or the modification declaration). Platforms MUST compare it only for equality and MUST NOT parse or order it.

cancel_operation.description: One requested operation. The same shape is used for whole-order and unit cancellation.

op.description: Operation. Only `cancel` is defined; the Business MUST reject any operation not declared for the target.

create_request.title: Create Modification Request
create_request.description: Body of the request that creates a modification attempt. State-changing: carries a signed Idempotency-Key. The Business assigns `modification_id` on admission.

base_order_version.description: The `order_version` against which the declaration was observed. A mismatch on a new attempt is rejected with `stale_order_state` before admission.

operations.description: One or more cancellation operations. Targets MUST be unique; an `order` target MUST NOT be combined with `unit` targets.

blocked_by.description: The dependency that prevented execution of a `not_attempted` operation.

type.description: Kind of blocker. Well-known values: `operation` (another operation in the same attempt; `target` identifies it) and `order_state` (current Order state). Platforms MUST tolerate unknown values.

target.description: The blocking operation's target when `type` is `operation`.

result.description: Authoritative outcome of one requested operation. Outcomes are not interchangeable: `awaiting_business_decision` implies no execution; `committed` implies the Order mutated but not that any refund completed.

op.description: The operation this result belongs to.

outcome.description: Well-known values: `awaiting_business_decision` (admitted, Business has not decided, nothing committed), `committed` (Order mutation committed; refund may still be pending), `refused` (Business declined before any mutation), `failed` (execution conclusively did not commit), `indeterminate` (whether execution committed is not yet authoritative; MUST NOT be used merely because approval is pending), `not_attempted` (execution did not start because of the dependency in `blocked_by`). Platforms MUST treat any unrecognized value as unresolved and not successful.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason. Required for `refused` and `failed`. Well-known: `refused_by_policy`, `unit_unavailable`, `conflicting_modification`, `stale_eligibility`.

affected_amount.description: Non-negative amount attributed to the target by a committed operation. Not the signed financial amount of any adjustment and not evidence a refund completed.

adjustments.description: IDs of Order `adjustments[]` entries created or updated by this result. The Order `adjustments[]` array, not this result, is authoritative for refund and credit status.

decided_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the Business reached the outcome, when known.

modification_record.title: Modification
modification_record.description: Durable record of one admitted modification attempt. Authoritative for attempt-level status; the Order read remains authoritative for current Order and adjustment state. A cached replay of this record is not a substitute for reading it again.

modification_id.description: Durable Business-assigned identifier of the attempt.

base_order_version.description: The version the original request was admitted against. Immutable.

atomicity.description: Commitment model that governed this attempt; copied from the declaration at admission. Well-known values: `atomic`, `per_unit`; unrecognized values are handled as in `modification.atomicity`.

status.description: Request-level aggregate derived from `results`. `open`: at least one result is `awaiting_business_decision`, `indeterminate`, or an unrecognized outcome. `closed`: every result is one of the terminal outcomes `committed`, `refused`, `failed`, or `not_attempted`. Platforms MUST treat unrecognized values as `open`.

results.description: One result per requested operation, in request order.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the attempt was admitted.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent change to any result.

retained_until.description: Until when the Business guarantees this record and its scoped-key association remain retrievable by `get_modification` and scoped lookup. MUST be at least 24 hours after `created_at` (the replay-cache minimum) and MAY be longer; the two lifetimes are separate contracts. Within this lifetime a scoped lookup MUST return `found`; after it lookup and fence MUST answer `unresolved` with `reason_code: record_expired`. The Business MUST keep a permanent claim marker for every claimed key, so a key it claimed is never fenced after the record expires.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Monetary amount in the currency's minor unit as defined by ISO 4217. Refer to the currency's exponent to determine minor-to-major ratio (e.g., 2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD).
